decision: How should the home page show the offer '30% off your first month' (CAD 69.30, then CAD 99 a month)?
primary_axis: where the offer lives and what carries it: price, page chrome, hero, coupon, or charge timing
invariants: real home page (/) with real copy and sections
math plan only, CAD 99 a month
visual only: checkout and Stripe still charge CAD 99
run: npm run dev, then open /?variant=A..E (floating bar or left/right arrow keys)

options.name: Price card: struck price
options.bet: The card leads with the first-month price: chip, CAD 99 struck, CAD 69.30 big, 'Then CAD 99 a month'. Hero fact line says the same
options.benefit: Most direct; the discount is the number a parent sees
options.cost: The big number is not the price they pay every month
options.risk: Reads as a CAD 69.30 product; the jump to 99 can feel like a bait

options.name: Announcement bar
options.bet: A dark bar above the nav on every load; pricing card adds one line
options.benefit: Seen first, on every page view; card stays honest at CAD 99
options.cost: Adds chrome above the nav; banner blindness
options.risk: Looks like a generic promo site

options.name: Hero sticker
options.bet: A round yellow sticker on the hero photo; pricing card adds one line
options.benefit: Playful, fits a kids' product, visible above the fold
options.risk: Feels like a retail sale sticker; less trust

options.name: Coupon stub
options.bet: A tear-off coupon joined to the plan card with a dashed edge: '30% off, CAD 69.30, added at checkout, no code'
options.benefit: Clear that it is a one-time extra; card price stays CAD 99
options.cost: Only in the pricing section; the hero says nothing
options.risk: Coupon metaphor can look cheap if overused

options.name: Charge timeline
options.bet: The card shows when money moves: Today CAD 0, first book ships CAD 69.30, every month after CAD 99
options.benefit: Answers 'when do I pay what' in one look; matches the real charge timing (D-053)
options.risk: Parents scanning for a deal can miss it
